name: virtualization_inventory
description: List the VMs, the disk files they name, the snapshots and the datastores that configuration files and inventory exports say exist, from a directory or a list of files. It reads, from their public descriptions and no others: VMware .vmx and .vmsd and ESXi's vmInventory.xml; a libvirt domain XML (devices, disks, backing stores), domain snapshot XML and storage pool XML; a Proxmox VM or container configuration (/etc/pve/qemu-server/<id>.conf, with its snapshot sections; a [special:...] section, such as the cloud-init settings, is listed as special and not as a snapshot) and storage.cfg. A Hyper-V (.vmcx, .vmrs), VirtualBox (.vbox), OVF or VMware template or state file is recognised and listed as unsupported, never guessed at, and a file of no recognised kind is counted by extension. Every record carries its source file id and the line or XML element it came from; versions are the strings the files carry (hardware version, machine type), and what they mean for a release is not stated. A disk a configuration names is looked up only among the files given: `in_set` no is a statement about the set, a hypervisor storage volume is listed and not looked up, and a configuration entry does not show that a VM ran, still exists or was not deleted. A time is derived only where the file states an epoch (Proxmox snaptime, libvirt creationTime, UTC by definition); the two raw fields of a .vmsd are kept raw and not decoded. XML is read with every DOCTYPE and entity declaration refused and the element count and depth bounded; text is read a line at a time with a line cap; a file over max_file_bytes is named and not read; a file with more than 100000 records is partial and says so. An XML file in an encoding the reader does not know fails that file and the run goes on. A Proxmox configuration names its first 200 snapshot and special sections with their totals; every snapshot section is a row of snapshots, paged whole. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`, the pair the recipes' coverage.json carries; exit 0 means the engine ran, not that the examination is complete. SENSITIVE: a configuration can hold a console password, a cloud-init password, an SSH key or a user-data blob under a key this tool does not show: only a fixed list of keys is shown, every other key is counted, and the names (not values) of those that look like credentials are listed with their line, their section and the length of the value, in every section they sit in; a libvirt console password attribute is named to a cap of 200 and counted past it. SENSITIVE: names, paths and values the answer shows pass a shape check (a token-shaped run and user-info are withheld, a text over 512 characters is shown cut with its whole length, and nothing is cut or folded before it is checked; a piece of a path such as a datastore or a node is taken from the path after the whole was checked); every key and value of the answer, an error answer and every paging-file row passes one way out that withholds by shape again (user-info up to the last `@` before the host, a secret right after `=`, the value after a name such as password=, secret: or AccountKey=, prefixes such as glpat-, sk_live_ and SG., a run or an integer of more than 18 digits; only the exact names of the files this run made are shown as they are), then reads back what it wrote and checks it by the same rules and by a second check written apart from them (a PEM marker, a named secret, a long digit run, a known token prefix, user-info and a random-looking run, each after zero-width and control characters are removed), replacing a string either would change by <withheld: N bytes>, listing its place and the check in boundary.replaced_at, and making the answer partial; an extension that is not 1 to 10 letters or digits is counted under (other extensions). A secret that does not look like a token is not recognised, so run it as a job with secret_output: true. write_text: true (refused outside a job) creates $OUT/inventory-values.jsonl, mode 0600, created before anything is read, holding the originals; a file already there is refused by name.

root.description: A directory of the evidence files (a link is refused; links inside it are listed and never followed). Give root, paths, or both

paths.description: Files named one by one (a link or a special file is named and never opened)

limit.description: Rows shown inline per list (default 200); every row is counted and, when there are more, the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.<list>.all_results

max_files.description: The most files taken into the set (default 20000, at most 200000); past it the answer is partial and says where the walk stopped

max_entries.description: The most directory entries listed (default 200000, at most 2000000)

max_depth.description: How deep the walk goes (default 16, at most 64); a deeper directory is named

max_seconds.description: The time to spend (default 50, at most 50); what is left is named and the answer is partial

write_text.description: Write the original of every name or value the answer shows withheld or shortened to one 0600 file under $OUT (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true

max_file_bytes.description: A file over this many bytes is named and not read (default 16777216, at most 268435456); nothing is cut
